heading: Definitions
lead: For the purpose of this subchapter—

tree.text: “agency” means an Executive agency and a military department;

“employee” means an employee in or under an agency who is a citizen or national of the United States or an alien admitted to the United States for permanent residence, but does not include a part-time or intermittent employee or native labor casually hired on an hourly or daily basis. However, such an employee who enters a status listed in paragraph (5)(A)–(E) of this section— is an employee for the purpose of this subchapter only on a determination by the head of the agency concerned that this status is the proximate result of employment by the agency;

children.text: inside the continental United States; or

who is a resident at or in the vicinity of his place of employment in a territory or possession of the United States or in a foreign country and who was not living there solely as a result of his employment;
an unmarried child (including an unmarried dependent stepchild or adopted child) under 21 years of age;
a dependent designated in official rec­ords; and
an individual determined to be dependent by the head of the agency concerned or his designee;

tree.text: “active service” means active Federal service by an employee;

“missing status” means the status of an employee who is in active service and is officially carried or determined to be absent in a status of— but does not include the status of an employee for a period during which he is officially determined to be absent from his post of duty without authority; and

children.text: captured, beleaguered, or besieged by a hostile force; or
detained in a foreign country against his will;
station per diem allowances for not more than 90 days.

notes.heading: Effective Date of 1997 Amendment
notes.text: Pub. L. 105–85, div. A, title VI, § 603(e), Nov. 18, 1997, 111 Stat. 1783, provided that: “This section [amending this section, sections 708, 2830, 2882, 7572, and 7573 of Title 10, Armed Forces, section 107 of Title 32, National Guard, sections 101, 403, 405, 406, 420, 427, 551, and 1014 of Title 37, Pay and Allowances of the Uniformed Services, and section 3803 of Title 50, War and National Defense, repealing section 403a of Title 37, and enacting provisions set out as a note under section 403 of Title 37] and the amendments made by this section shall take effect on January 1, 1998.”

notes.heading: Accounting for Civilian Employees and Contractors of United States
notes.text: Pub. L. 104–106, div. A, title V, § 569(e), Feb. 10, 1996, 110 Stat. 352, directed Secretary of State to carry out comprehensive study of provisions of this subchapter and any other law or regulation establishing procedures for accounting for civilian employees of the United States or contractors of the United States who serve with or accompany the Armed Forces in the field to determine the means, if any, by which those procedures may be improved, and further provided for submission of report to Congress not later than one year after Feb. 10, 1996, on results of study.

notes.heading: Benefits for United States Hostages in Iraq and Kuwait and United States Hostages Captured in Lebanon
notes.text: Pub. L. 101–513, title V, § 599C, Nov. 5, 1990, 104 Stat. 2064, as amended by Pub. L. 102–138, title III, § 302(a), Oct. 28, 1991, 105 Stat. 707; Pub. L. 102–499, § 5(a), Oct. 24, 1992, 106 Stat. 3266, provided for payment of benefits during fiscal year 1991 and thereafter for United States hostages in Iraq and Kuwait and United States hostages captured in Lebanon.

notes.heading: Hostage Relief
notes.text: Pub. L. 96–449, Oct. 14, 1980, 94 Stat. 1967, as amended by Pub. L. 99–514, § 2, Oct. 22, 1986, 100 Stat. 2095; Pub. L. 102–83, § 5(c)(2), Aug. 6, 1991, 105 Stat. 406, known as the “Hostage Relief Act of 1980”, provided for benefits for United States civil service and uniformed service personnel who were placed in a captive status during a hostage period beginning on Nov. 4, 1979, due to the seizure of the United States Embassy in Iran.

notes.heading: Executive Order No. 12268
notes.text: Ex. Ord. No. 12268, Jan. 15, 1981, 46 F.R. 4671, provided for the implementation of the Hostage Relief Act of 1980 (Pub. L. 96–449).

notes.heading: Executive Order No. 12313
notes.text: Ex. Ord. No. 12313, July 13, 1981, 46 F.R. 36689, designated Jan. 11, 1981, as date on which all citizens and resident aliens of the United States who had been placed in captive status as a result of seizure of United States Embassy in Iran were returned to United States or otherwise accounted for and were no longer under foreign control.
